name: Plumping gloss (menthol / cinnamon)
lead: Plumping gloss is a lip product that makes lips look fuller and softer for a few hours. People use it as a quick, non-invasive way to get a fuller, glossier lip line without fillers, and it can be applied over or instead of lipstick. Plumping glosses are often called lifter glosses, and they typically add a tingling, warming or cooling sensation when first applied. [1]

According to Wikipedia, these products work by irritating the skin of the lips, with ingredients such as capsaicin, which causes mild swelling and a temporarily fuller appearance. [2] Wikipedia's lip gloss article adds that plumping glosses can leave a burning sensation on first application, and that a similar illusion of fullness can be created with a cooling ingredient such as menthone glycerin acetal. [1] Menthol and cinnamon are other flavour-and-sensation ingredients commonly associated with such products; menthol activates the cold-sensing TRPM8 channel in sensory nerves. [3]

Wikipedia describes plumping glosses as a cheap and usually harmless alternative to collagen, hyaluronic-acid or fat injections, though less effective because the result is temporary. [1] No clinical studies of irritant plumping glosses were found.

chain: Gloss containing a warming, cooling or irritant ingredient is applied
Lip skin becomes mildly irritated, with swelling and increased blood flow
Lips look fuller and glossier for a short time
angle.text: Users apply the gloss on bare lips or over lip colour to get an immediate fuller, more defined look. The effect appears within minutes and fades as the sensation wears off, so it is used day to day or for photos and events rather than as a lasting change.

infobox: Skin irritation causing temporary swelling; cooling agents add a sensation of fullness [1][2]
Capsaicin, menthol or menthone derivatives, cinnamon, flavourings [1][2]

paras: Lip gloss is a cosmetic that gives lips a glossy lustre and sometimes a subtle colour. It is a mixture of waxes, oils and pigments with fewer pigments than lipstick, and its main components include lanolin and polybutene. [1] Plumping versions add ingredients meant to make lips look softer and fuller. [1]

Wikipedia's lip plumper article groups these products with suction devices that cause temporary swelling by drawing blood into the lips, and places them in a wider history of lip augmentation that includes paraffin injections around 1900, liquid silicone from the 1960s, bovine collagen from about 1980 and fat transfer. [2]

Wikipedia states that plumpers work by irritating lip skin, for example with capsaicin, the compound that gives chili peppers their heat, producing swelling and a temporarily fuller look. [2] Menthol-type ingredients act differently: menthol activates TRPM8, a cold- and menthol-sensing ion channel involved in thermosensation. [3] Products using cooling agents such as menthone glycerin acetal can create an impression of fullness. [1]

A randomised trial of oral capsaicin exposure found that repeated exposure reduced the response to capsaicin over time, a process called desensitisation. [4] That study concerned the mouth rather than lip cosmetics.

Wikipedia notes that lip glosses are generally considered safe when used as directed, but fragrances, flavourings, preservatives and colour additives can cause allergic reactions or irritation in sensitive people, with redness, dryness, itching or swelling of the lips. Shared applicators can harbour bacteria, and regulators set limits for contaminants such as lead in cosmetics. [1] Because plumping glosses work through irritation, burning or tingling on application is expected. [1][2]
No studies found for menthol, cinnamon or capsaicin plumping glosses. Laboratory and pharmacology research exists on the sensory channels these ingredients act on, such as TRPM8 for menthol. [3]

timeline.event: Max Factor invents lip gloss for film use. [1]
Max Factor's X-Rated, the first commercially available lip gloss, launches. [1]

refs.title: Inducible desensitization to capsaicin with repeated low-dose exposure in human volunteers.

card.summary: Irritant glosses that swell lips for a short-lived fuller look; little formal research behind them.

quick.overview:
Plumping glosses contain ingredients that irritate the lips, which temporarily swell and look fuller. The effect is short-lived.

No clinical studies were found.
quick.mechanism: Irritation of the lip skin produces mild swelling, according to Wikipedia.
quick.risks: Since the mechanism is irritation, redness or discomfort can be expected; no studies of adverse events specific to these products were found.
